summary: The article accurately reports on SEBI's recent simplifications for inheriting shares, including specific monetary limits and procedural changes, with only one minor discrepancy regarding the SEBI Chairman's name in the initial mention.

claims.claim: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey led a recent Board meeting that approved new rules to make inheriting shares much simpler.
claims.note: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey presided over the board meeting on June 19, 2026, where these reforms were approved.

claims.claim: The new rules, approved by the SEBI Board on June 19, 2026, aim to make this process much smoother, faster, and less burdensome for legal heirs.
claims.note: The SEBI Board approved the new framework for transmission of securities on June 19, 2026, with the aim of simplifying and expediting the process for legal heirs.

claims.claim: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey, who took office on March 1, 2025, for a three-year term, presided over a crucial SEBI Board meeting on June 19, 2026.
claims.note: Tuhin Kanta Pandey assumed office as the 11th Chairman of SEBI on March 1, 2025, for a three-year term. He presided over the SEBI Board meeting on June 19, 2026.

claims.claim: If the value of physical shares (shares held as paper certificates) is up to ₹10,000, or dematerialised (demat) shares (shares held electronically in a demat account) is up to ₹30,000, families can now claim them with minimal documentation.
claims.note: SEBI introduced Quick Transmission Processing (QTP) for small-value claims, specifically up to ₹10,000 for physical holdings and up to ₹30,000 for dematerialised holdings, with minimal documentation.

claims.claim: Earlier, for physical shares, simplified documentation was allowed up to ₹5 lakh. This limit has now been doubled to ₹10 lakh. For demat holdings, the limit has been increased from ₹15 lakh to ₹30 lakh.
claims.note: The limits for simplified documentation have been doubled from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh for physical holdings and from ₹15 lakh to ₹30 lakh for dematerialised holdings.

claims.claim: Importantly, SEBI has removed the requirement for a Permanent Account Number (PAN) and mandatory probate of wills for these simplified processes.
claims.note: SEBI has removed the requirement to submit PAN and the mandatory requirement of probate of wills for these simplified processes.

article_title: Easier Days for Families: SEBI Simplifies Inheriting Shares
